concepts.def: Data collected first-hand by the researcher through surveys, interviews, observation or experiments.
Existing data: official statistics, historical documents, media content, analysed by someone other than the original collector.
Approach favouring quantitative, statistical methods; treats society like a natural science object; Durkheim's suicide study (1897).
Favours qualitative, in-depth methods to access meanings; Weber's 'verstehen' (understanding).
Using multiple methods to cross-check findings; e.g. combining surveys and interviews.
In-depth participant observation of a group; e.g. Whyte (1943) Street Corner Society of an Italian-American gang.
